changeability.rationale: The classic bugs (sprite URL, species mapping, caching) each land in one obvious place; only small presentation-level fallbacks are copy-pasted between move and ability pages.

evidence: app/src/main.ts:17-24 — pages are looked up through a narrow (params, url) => Promise<Node> contract
app/src/api.ts:10,108-111 — fetching and caching are centralized; pages never touch fetch or URLs directly

coupling.rationale: Client/server are cleanly separated and pages depend on narrow helpers, but the route table exists in two places and a couple of data-shaping rules are duplicated between pages and the api layer.

evidence: app/src/dom.ts:38-52 — section() with aria-labelledby is a real, reused abstraction; app/src/components.ts:27-41 — pokemonCard's `extra` slot absorbs home's type badges and ability's hidden note without flags
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:138-160 — moves tables are driven by a declarative COLUMNS/Column spec, so new columns are one entry
app/src/pages/move.ts:15 — the `fact` dl helper is private to move.ts; an Items page copies it, as does pokemon.ts's measurements dl
app/src/api.ts:211 — toSpeciesCards' {pokemon: NamedRef} contract forces move.ts:6 to map learned_by_pokemon into wrapper objects
app/src/main.ts:17-24 — adding a route is one table entry, but a second regex in server.mjs:32 is needed
abstraction_design.rationale: The shared pieces (h/section, cards, cached get, COLUMNS spec) are designed around the app's real variation and stretch nicely, but they stop just short of a reusable 'resource detail page' shape: adding Items means copying the facts-dl and effect-fallback snippets rather than reusing them.

findings.issue: The client route table (app/src/main.ts:17-24) is duplicated as a second regex list in the production server; every route added, renamed or removed must be changed in both files or the server serves 404s (or wrongly 200s) for it.
findings.suggestion: Export the route patterns from a module both sides import (the server can import from src since it's plain regexes), or at least add a comment in each file pointing at its twin.

findings.issue: The English short_effect → flavor-text → em-dash fallback is duplicated verbatim in app/src/pages/ability.ts:8-10; a fix to the whitespace handling or fallback order lands twice.
findings.suggestion: Extract an `englishEffect(effectEntries, flavorEntries)` helper into api.ts next to latestFlavorText().

findings.issue: The type-label fallback `types.get(name) ?? humanize(name)` appears at four call sites (pokemon.ts:62, pokemon.ts:296, move.ts:25, types.ts:54).
findings.suggestion: Add a `typeLabel(names, name)` helper (or make typeNames() resolve labels) so the fallback lives once.

findings.issue: The non-type exclusion list ['stellar','unknown','shadow'] is hardcoded twice: once in api.ts:185's allTypes() filter and once here as a NotFound guard.
findings.suggestion: Export the list from api.ts (e.g. `NON_TYPES`) and use it in both places.

findings.issue: toSpeciesCards' `{ pokemon: NamedRef }` item contract (chosen so ability.ts can keep is_hidden) forces the move page to re-wrap learned_by_pokemon entries into single-key objects.
findings.suggestion: Give toSpeciesCards an overload/param that accepts NamedRef[] directly, or have it accept an item→NamedRef selector.

findings.issue: The per-species types-by-slot and generation-membership aggregates are built inline in the home page; any other page needing the same mapping (e.g. a future dex view) would copy ~20 lines.
findings.suggestion: Move typesById/generationById construction into api.ts as named aggregates alongside speciesIndex().

findings.issue: section() names headings with a module-global incrementing counter, so element ids churn between renders and are non-deterministic across loads.
findings.suggestion: Derive the id from a slug of the title, or accept a caller-supplied id when stable anchors matter.

summary: This is a small, tidy codebase with real seams: routes are one table entry, data fetching/caching is one function, and every Pokémon card flows through a single component, so the highest-risk fixes (sprites, species mapping) land in exactly one place. The main frictions are the route list duplicated between client and server, and a handful of small copy-pasted presentation snippets (effect fallback, type-label fallback, facts dl) that would multiply if a fourth resource type like Items is added. Overall it reads like code a reviewer would happily maintain with minor nudges.
